title: Nick and Joe Jonas Snack on Bhajia, Kachori, and Papad During Tour Break
excerpt: The Jonas Brothers continue to embrace Indian cuisine on their 20th anniversary tour, with Nick's love for Indian food now a recurring highlight of their social media presence.
body:
• Nick and Joe Jonas were spotted enjoying bhajia, kachori, and papad during a break on their Jonas20 anniversary tour
  • Nick Jonas, married to Priyanka Chopra, has become known for his love of Indian food — from paneer and biryani to dosas at breakfast buffets
  • The Jonas Brothers have been using Bollywood tracks like Shararat and Aavan Jaavan as pre-show hype music on the current tour

Nick and Joe Jonas took an Indian food detour during their ongoing Jonas20: Greetings from Your Hometown Tour, sharing their spread of bhajia, kachori, and papad with fans. The snack break is the latest in a long line of Indian food moments that have made Nick Jonas — married to Priyanka Chopra since 2018 — a beloved figure among Indian fans worldwide.

From Concert Stages to Indian Snack Plates

The Jonas Brothers are in the middle of their 20th anniversary tour, which has taken them across the United States, South America, and into Canada this August, with recent stops including Thackerville, Oklahoma on August 1, Mount Pleasant, Michigan on August 5, and Oro-Medonte, Canada on August 7. Between concert performances, the brothers have been documenting their food adventures on social media, and Indian cuisine keeps making appearances.

The specific snacks — bhajia (deep-fried vegetable fritters), kachori (stuffed and fried pastry), and papad (thin, crispy lentil wafers) — are staples of Indian street food culture and Gujarati-Rajasthani snack traditions. Their appearance on a Jonas Brothers tour stop drew immediate attention from Indian fans and media.

Nick Jonas: India's 'National Jiju'

Nick Jonas's relationship with Indian food has been well-documented since his marriage to actress Priyanka Chopra in a grand ceremony in Rajasthan in December 2018. In interviews and fan interactions, he has named paneer, lamb biryani, and dosa as his favorite Indian dishes. Priyanka herself has confirmed that "Nick's favourite Indian food is any kind of paneer."

Earlier this year, Nick went viral with an Instagram video titled "When they have dosa at the breakfast buffet," showing him digging into crispy dosa with evident delight while a Bollywood track played in the background. The video drew thousands of comments, with fans dubbing him "more Indian than most Indians" and celebrating "the jijufication of Nick Jonas."

"Never in my Disney Jonas Brothers-obsessed era did I imagine that 20 years later, Nick Jonas would be eating dosa and fully adapting to Indian culture. Life really said plot twists!"

— Fan comment on Instagram

Bollywood Music as Pre-Show Ritual

The food moments are part of a broader pattern of the Jonas Brothers embracing Indian culture on tour. Nick has been sharing clips of the trio grooving to Bollywood tracks before taking the stage — first Aavan Jaavan from War 2, which drew reactions from Hrithik Roshan and Kiara Advani, and then Shararat from the Ranveer Singh-starrer Dhurandhar.

During filming for Camp Rock 3 in Vancouver earlier this year, Nick was spotted twice at Desi Indian Lounge, a modern Indian restaurant on Hornby Street. His order included Kerala Chicken Pepper, Paneer Tikka, Paneer Butter Masala, and Biryani — a spread that leaned heavily into the restaurant's contemporary Indian menu.

Why It Resonates With the Diaspora

For Indian Americans and the broader diaspora, Nick Jonas's unforced enthusiasm for Indian food has become a cultural touchpoint. His willingness to share these moments publicly — eating kachori backstage, playing Bollywood songs before shows, visiting Indian restaurants repeatedly — goes beyond celebrity novelty. It reflects a genuine integration of Indian food culture into his daily life, driven by his marriage to one of India's biggest film stars.

The Jonas Brothers' tour continues through August 2026, and if the pattern holds, expect more Indian snack sightings from the road.
nri_angle: Nick Jonas's genuine embrace of Indian food and Bollywood culture has made him a beloved figure among the Indian diaspora, turning casual snack moments into cultural touchpoints.
author: Diaspora Desk
